post.summary: Approve and send the campaign now
post.description: Records who approved it. Each customer is checked for opt-out and consent immediately before their email is sent. Calling again never sends twice: a sent campaign returns its results, one being sent returns 409 send_in_progress, and an interrupted send resumes with the customers not yet handled. 409 sender_incomplete: add a mailing address in Settings. 503 email_not_configured: email is not set up for this environment.

post.summary: Unsubscribe from a business’s emails (the page linked in every email footer)
post.description: No account needed. The front-end page at /unsubscribe reads the token from the URL fragment and posts it here. Stops all future email from that business to that address. Idempotent.

post.summary: One-click unsubscribe used by mail apps (List-Unsubscribe header)
post.description: Not for front ends. Same effect as POST /v1/public/unsubscribe.

post.summary: Import customers and their last service from a CSV file
post.description: Send the file contents as `csv`. Run with mode "preview" first: nothing is saved and you get a report. Then send the same file with mode "import". Columns (header names are flexible): name (required), email, phone, address, address2, city, state, zip, notes, service_type, last_service_date (YYYY-MM-DD or MM/DD/YYYY), interval_days. One row per customer, or several rows per customer for several past services. Existing customers are matched by customer_id, email, or name + address and never overwritten; services already on file are skipped, so re-importing a file is safe. Import is all-or-nothing unless skip_invalid_rows is true (400 import_has_errors). At most 5000 rows. Contact permissions are not imported; record those separately.

parameters.name: x-organization-id
parameters.description: Organization (workspace) context. The server verifies your membership.

customers_matched.description: Rows that matched an existing customer (nothing overwritten).

service_records_duplicate.description: Already on file (same customer, service and date).

applied.description: True only when mode was "import" and the rows were saved.

get.description: One row per service record; customers without any appear once. The file re-imports cleanly. Cells that a spreadsheet would treat as formulas are prefixed with an apostrophe.
